name: Unigood Tech Smart Table Rate Shipping
author: unigoodtech

sections.description:
Unigood Tech Smart Table Rate Shipping evaluates deterministic rules per shipping-method instance. It includes a structured rule editor, simulator, immutable revisions, and recoverable preview-before-commit JSON/CSV portability.

No telemetry, remote calls, licence calls or AI calls are made.

The complete human-readable PHP, JavaScript and CSS source is included in the plugin. No compilation, minification or external build tools are required.

Source Code

All deployed PHP, JavaScript and CSS files are supplied in human-readable form in this plugin package. There are no generated or minified production assets and no build step is required to modify or redistribute the plugin.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate WooCommerce 10.8 or newer.
  2. Upload and activate this plugin.
  3. Open WooCommerce > Settings > Shipping > Shipping zones.
  4. Add “Unigood Tech Smart Table Rate”.
  5. Configure title, tax status, matching mode and validated rules.
sections.faq:
What happens if no rule matches?

This method returns no rate. Configure another zone method if a fallback is required.

Is data deleted on uninstall?

Configuration is preserved by default. An authorised administrator can explicitly opt into plugin-scoped deletion during uninstall from a shipping-method instance. Deactivation never deletes data.

0.6.5

  • Replace short runtime, storage, AJAX, asset and namespace prefixes with a unique Unigood Tech prefix.
  • Canonically sanitise imported, posted and restored rule fields before validation and storage.
  • Preserve the existing portable-file schema for v0.6.4 export compatibility.

0.6.4

  • Rename the public plugin identity and text domain to Unigood Tech Smart Table Rate Shipping following the WordPress.org trademark pre-review.
  • Preserve the established method ID, PHP namespace, code prefixes and stored-data keys for upgrade compatibility.

0.6.3

  • Complete Plugin Check corrective release: direct nonce verification in every AJAX action, explicit numeric input sanitisation, translator context for placeholders, stream-free canonical CSV handling, and documented one-time uninstall queries.
  • Retain WordPress 7.1 compatibility metadata required by the WordPress.org submission scanner.

0.6.2

  • Declare WooCommerce through the native WordPress plugin dependency header.
  • Enforce WooCommerce 10.8 or newer before registering functionality or loading administration assets.
  • Document that all deployed source is human-readable and requires no build tools.
  • Add privacy-reviewed screenshot captions for the WordPress.org listing.

0.6.1

  • Prevent a fatal error when the plugin is activated without WooCommerce.
  • Load administration assets only on WooCommerce Shipping settings screens.

0.6.0

  • Preserve all plugin data on deactivation and by default on uninstall.
  • Add an explicit, default-off uninstall deletion choice with capability checks and plugin-scoped cleanup.

0.5.2

  • Invalidate the commit control after a failed or stale import commit and require a fresh preview.

0.5.1

  • Show the downloadable error report only when an import error exists.

0.5.0

  • Export canonical UTF-8 JSON and formula-safe CSV without secrets or customer data.
  • Preview imports without mutation, reconcile by stable ID and report create/update/skip/retain counts.
  • Commit only after confirmation with concurrency protection, a recovery snapshot and immutable revision.

0.4.6

  • Show saved rule names, prices and cost changes on revision cards.
  • Mark the current revision and collapse technical details.

0.4.5

  • Bind revision history to the instance ID rendered in the WooCommerce method modal.
  • Preserve revision records written by v0.4.4.

0.4.4

  • Add immutable configuration revisions and restore-as-new-revision.
  • Add concurrency protection using the token stored in the live WooCommerce instance settings.
  • Retain WooCommerce’s native modal-save lifecycle.

0.3.0

  • Add a nonce-protected simulator for authorised WooCommerce administrators.
  • Show normalised synthetic inputs, condition results, matched and rejected rules, mode, cost components, rounding, taxes intent, final rate and elapsed time.
  • Keep simulation isolated from the live cart, checkout and saved configuration.

0.2.2

  • Keep unchecked rule-enabled controls visibly recognisable in the WooCommerce shipping modal.

0.2.1

  • Correct structured editor layout for WooCommerce’s narrow shipping-method modal.
  • Prevent horizontal overflow and clipped controls.

0.2.0

  • Add a keyboard-operable structured editor for Core rules, AND/OR groups and conditions.
  • Add clone, delete and move controls with safe JSON serialisation.
  • Retain JSON as an advanced representation rather than the ordinary merchant workflow.

0.1.3

  • Bind validation to the WooCommerce 11 shipping modal’s actual field and button patterns.
  • Load the inert validator throughout wp-admin; it activates only when the UGT rules field exists.

0.1.2

  • Load field-level validation by the stable WooCommerce settings page route.

0.1.1

  • Show an accessible field-level error before invalid rule JSON or negative costs can be submitted.
  • Preserve the invalid draft for correction while leaving the last valid configuration active.

0.1.0

  • Initial Core calculation proof and Shipping Zones integration checkpoint.
